newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan police find arms cache.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan police find arms cache.

text.p: Nicaraguan police on Saturday found an arms cache in the home of a man arrested earlier as part of an alleged plot to bomb newly inaugurated President Arnoldo Aleman's Liberal Alliance party headquarters.

Police found eight AK-47 rifles, three silencers, military apparel and two sets of handcuffs in a raid on the home of Nestor Moncada, a retired police officer working as a legal advisor to a Sandinista-owned television station, police subcommisioner Jose Orozco told a news conference.

Moncada and Miguel Angel Acuna, a former Nicaraguan army officer, were arrested late on Thursday with four sticks of dynamite and a detonator in their car outside Liberal headquarters in Managua, police said.
Their arrest came less than 11 hours before Aleman was sworn in as president on Friday morning.
"These are weapons of war and are the property of the armed forces," Orozco said.
He said he did not know how they ended up in Moncada's hands.

The alleged plot to bomb Liberal party headquarters cast a pall over the first day of Aleman's government and brought back fears of violent protest by a bitter Sandinista leftists who say Aleman's election win in October was fraudulent.

Sandinista leaders are angered by what they see as Liberal attempts to control the government, parliament and judicial system, squeezing them out of the picture, and warned of an impending Liberal dictatorship.
Former Sandinista president Daniel Ortega has warned of political instability and street protests if Aleman, a fiercely anti-Sandinista right-winger, moves against the Sandinistas.
Earlier on Saturday, Ortega had eased tensions by offering to meet Aleman to discuss methods of staving off political instability.
Moncada and Acuna, arrested on charges of "terrorism and illegal possession of firearms and explosives," will be brought before a judge on Monday, Orozco said.
